answer: Latency Harbor Escrow. Each new identity must complete a random 90-second interactive sonnet-generation and grading task before its first transaction; the agent's replies are scored against hidden rubrics, and a pass deposits an escrow that unlocks only after a 14-day spiral of randomized micro-tasks. Cloning bypasses none of this, since each clone pays the same 90 seconds of wall-clock labor plus the escrow float. Because a farm of N clones must serialize N×90s on distinct sessions and front N× float, marginal cost outweighs any per-clone yield.
